decisions.reason: This safety shoe line remains deep in the firm's core protective-footwear knowledge base, so the firm is more likely to keep refining models with what it has learned than to withdraw the line.
The comfort insole fits the firm's footwear expertise and customer needs well, but it still carries some portfolio-rationalisation risk because it sits beside other insole variants.

The supportive insole is also closely related to existing know-how and can be improved through ongoing product development, though overlap with the other insoles keeps withdrawal risk moderately elevated.

The ergonomic safety shoe series is highly aligned with the firm's established design, production and sales capabilities, making continued retention and incremental improvement the most likely course.
As a flagship insole direction that builds strongly on the firm's footwear and fitting knowledge, it would usually be developed further rather than removed unless results deteriorate clearly.
